content.value: Plugins extend Barkpark with data and behaviour — never UI — by riding the public `Barkpark.*` highway, and the host works fully with all of them off.

Every plugin implements the Plugin Behaviour: a documented Elixir behaviour that grants schemas, endpoints, and background work, but no bespoke UI. When a plugin needs an affordance the host lacks, the rule is to extend the host generically rather than smuggle in a one-off interface. The guarantee this buys is the Fresh Install Invariant — disable every plugin and Barkpark still serves content.

content.value: Not everything that extends Barkpark sits in the plugin registry. The Indx Engine is a retriever seam, not a registry plugin — its absence from the registry is correct by design (see Indx Retriever Seam). It rides the same
highway to extend Search without being a UI guest.
A registry plugin's new endpoints surface automatically through the Capabilities Manifest, so the bp CLI and Go TUI gain plugin commands with no client change.
